title: Build and Explore Your Windows Security Monitoring Lab
platform: Windows 11 · existing host or VMware guest
objective: Identify Windows Security audit records and preserve a usable event inventory.
setup: Use your own Windows 11 host directly, or start an existing Windows 11 guest in VMware on an isolated lab network. Event Viewer and Windows PowerShell are built in. Use an approved account with Security log access. Keep host account names and IPs out of exported evidence.
steps: Confirm which machine you are using and write down whether it is your Windows host or a VMware guest. A separate guest is optional for this read-only exercise.
Press Win+R, enter eventvwr.msc and press Enter. Expand Windows Logs and select Security.
Open Filter Current Log. Enter 4624,4634,4672 in the Event IDs field and apply it. If the filter is empty, broaden the time range or use the downloadable sample below.

Open a record. In General or Details, record its timestamp, Event ID, event source and a summary. Repeat for at least three records. For 4624, note Logon Type if present and distinguish type 2 (interactive) from type 3 (network).

Run the read-only PowerShell query to compare the XML-backed event records with the Event Viewer list. A 4672 record identifies special privileges associated with a new logon. It does not itself establish a separate interactive sign-in.
Save a redacted table or screenshot, then summarize a difference between the authentication, privilege and sign-out records in your notes.
command:
# Windows Run dialog
eventvwr.msc

# Windows PowerShell with approved Security log access
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4624,4634,4672} -MaxEvents 10 | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,ProviderName
sample:
09:00 4624 Logon user=analyst type=2
09:01 4672 Special logon user=analyst
09:06 4634 Logoff user=analyst
expected: The Authentication and Security audit provider normally shows Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing. 4624 records a successful sign-in, 4634 records a session ending, and 4672 identifies special privileges. Event Viewer timestamps may be shown in local time.
troubleshoot: If access is denied, reopen PowerShell or Event Viewer with approved elevated access, or switch to your lab guest. If no matching log exists, read the supplied transcript and label your results sample-based. Do not change host auditing policy for this exercise.
evidence: Save a redacted table of at least three Security records.
checklist: Owned Windows host, isolated guest, or sample verified
Event Viewer Security log or sample reviewed
Three records documented with timestamp and source
Event IDs distinguished in notes
Redacted evidence saved

title: Read Linux System Logs
platform: Ubuntu, Debian, or Kali with systemd
objective: Find authentication and service records in the systemd journal and identify their origin.
setup: Start an owned Linux guest with systemd. journalctl is installed with systemd. In a non-systemd VM, review the practice artifact using a text editor.
steps: Run the journalctl command and read the timestamp, host, and program identifier in each entry.
If you have approved elevation, run sudo true, which performs no work, and rerun the sudo-specific query.
Compare the journal entry with the sample and classify three records by program and operation.
Save a redacted event inventory.
command:
journalctl -b -n 20 --no-pager -o short-iso
sudo true
journalctl -b -t sudo -n 10 --no-pager -o short-iso
sample:
07:02 sudo analyst : COMMAND=/usr/bin/true
07:03 systemd Started user manager
07:04 sshd Accepted publickey for analyst
expected: The first query shows records from the current boot. Successful elevation may produce sudo command and session records, depending on logging policy.
troubleshoot: If journald reports restricted access, use approved admin access in the lab or work from the sample. Under non-systemd environments use the downloadable excerpt.
evidence: Save a three-row journal inventory with timestamps and program names.
checklist: Located and checked the sudo evidence
Classify the program name, operation and principal in three journal entries.
Save a three-row journal inventory with timestamps and program names.
